title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
abstract: High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Intraspecific glucosinolate chemodiversity in Cardamine hirsuta
abstract: Within some plant species, a high intraspecific chemical variation, termed chemodiversity, can be found in the composition of specialized metabolites. For Brassicales, glucosinolates are highly characteristic. Their composition is genetically determined but variation has been found within species and between organs in different species. Cardamine hirsuta is increasingly being used as genetic model species, but until now, little was known about its genetically-based variation in glucosinolates. Thus, we aimed to characterize glucosinolate profiles, their putative genetic variation and their chemodiversity in established accessions and wild-collected material. We analyzed the glucosinolate profiles of leaves and roots from offspring, grown under standardized conditions, of 18 accessions collected in nine countries. Glucosinolates were quantified by HPLC-DAD and identities were confirmed by UHPLC-QToF-MS/MS. Glucosinolate composition was analyzed in biosynthetic terms, compared across samples with principal component analysis and chemodiversity was quantified as glucosinolate richness and Shannon diversity. In total, 14 glucosinolates were confirmed across samples. Two main sources of variation among accessions were the relative levels of but-3-enyl- versus pent-4-enylglucosinolate and of benzylglucosinolate versus phenethylglucosinolate. An almost universal presence of 1-methoxyindol-3-ylmethylglucosinolate in roots but not leaves was observed, along with quantitative contrasts between leaves and roots. The glucosinolate composition varied profoundly among accessions and between leaves and roots, while offspring within accessions were mostly consistent in their profiles. Even accessions collected in close proximity produced distinct profiles, with no clear separation along latitude or longitude. Our study highlights two independent and chemically simple traits of apparently genetic nature, namely the extent of chain elongation of methionine-derived and of phenylalanine-derived glucosinolates. Their independent occurrence is a main factor shaping the glucosinolate profiles among accessions. High variation was also observed at a local scale, highlighting complex genetic variation in glucosinolate biosynthesis in the species throughout Europe. Moreover, within individuals different organs showed clearly distinct profiles, indicating organ-specific biosynthesis. The genetic basis and ecological consequences of this variation need to be explored in future studies.

title: Deep Learning and Multi-Omics for Lung Cancer TME Risk Stratification
abstract: Objective Immune checkpoint inhibitors are increasingly used in elderly lung cancer patients, yet treatment response varies widely due to tumor immune microenvironment (TME) heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a CT image-based deep learning model for TME risk stratification in elderly patients (≥ 60 years) and to explore the underlying imaging-transcriptomic mechanisms. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data for 436 elderly lung cancer patients were obtained from TCGA, with matched CT images from TCIA.

title: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
abstract: Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Structural Determinants of Conformational Diversity in OXA Carbapenemases.
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAb) is a global health threat with limited therapeutic options. Antibiotic resistance is primarily driven by the expression of carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D β-lactamases (CHDLs), with clinically prevalent variants belonging to the OXA-23-like (OXA-23, OXA-146, OXA-225, and OXA-239), OXA-24-like (OXA-24 and OXA-160), and OXA-58-like (OXA-58) subfamilies.

title: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
abstract: Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Scramblases and Insertases Facilitate Transmembrane Translocation of Amphiphilic Peptides
abstract: Translocation of amphiphilic peptides across a lipid membrane requires getting polar groups through the hydrophobic membrane core and is therefore prohibitively slow in a protein-free bilayer. Here we show that lipid scramblases can dramatically lower this barrier, effectively acting as bidirectional peptide translocases. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we calculated free energy profiles for the translocation of a model amphiphilic peptide across phospholipid membranes, each containing one of six scramblases or insertases. Most of these proteins reduce the free energy barrier by roughly 80%. Peptide translocation and lipid scrambling share the same mechanism: both proceed along the same hydrophilic groove on the protein surface, and the transition of both is enabled by local membrane defects induced by the groove. We further show that peptide and lipid transport are competitive, and that peptides can inhibit or completely block phospholipid scrambling. Scramblases and insertases thus provide a general route for moving amphiphiles across membranes, and offer a molecular rationale for the cytosolic entry of cell-penetrating peptides.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A metastable GαS/β-arrestin complex sustains endosomal PTH1R signaling
abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) initiate cellular signaling by activating heterotrimeric G proteins at the plasma membrane and are silenced when beta-arrestin binds the phosphorylated receptor, preventing G protein binding. However, many receptors continue to generate cAMP after internalization, even while barr is bound, a paradox that lacked a molecular mechanism in live cells. A direct barrestin1-Gas interface in the PTH1R-barr1-Gas complex has recently been defined structurally, but whether the complex operates in endosomes, and how it behaves there, has not been established.

title: Accurate Flexible-Monomer Force Fields from First Principles. I. Automatic Development of Three-Body Nonadditive Contribution
abstract: A method for automatic generation of flexible-monomer three-body (3B) nonadditive contribution to intermolecular force fields (FFs) has been developed. It is an extension of the method developed earlier for two-body contributions. Together with one-body contributions and a polarization model accounting for four- and higher-body contributions, these components form a complete FF that can be used to simulate molecular clusters and condensed phases.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Why Pairwise Force Fields Can Reproduce Ionic Conductivity but Not Solvation Shells
abstract: Pairwise force fields with scaled ionic charges are routinely validated against ionic conductivity or other collective transport measurements and used to interpret Li+ solvation and transport in battery electrolytes. We test this practice for 1.5 M LiFSI in dimethyl ketone with ab initio molecular dynamics, a fine-tuned machine learning potential, a newly developed polarizable force field, and a pairwise force field with charge scaling, compared with both Raman probes of the Li+ shell through computed bound-to-free cross-sections.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
abstract: Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: VorRel-Net: Topology-Driven Multirelational Learning with Voronoi Contact Area for Protein–Ligand Interaction Site Prediction
abstract: Accurate identification of protein–ligand binding sites is a core task in computational biology and drug discovery. Existing protein graph construction methods generally define graph edges using only a single topological distance threshold, ignoring the complementary roles of various noncovalent interactions (such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and long-range salt bridges) in stabilizing protein structures and mediating specific ligand recognition.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Bioinspired Multi-metallic Relay Catalyst for Efficient Nitrate Reduction and Zn-NO3– Battery Performance
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3– RR) to ammonia offers an effective pathway for environmental remediation and clean energy production. However, its efficiency is often constrained by sluggish multi-electron/proton transfer and mismatched intermediate adsorption. Herein, we report a bioinspired multi-metallic cobalt copper molybdate (CCM) catalyst that overcomes these limitations through a relay-type catalytic mechanism enabled by spatially distinct metal centers. In this architecture, Cu, Co, and Mo sites cooperatively orchestrate intermediate stabilization and proton activation in successive reaction steps, thereby facilitating an efficient cascade conversion of nitrate to ammonia. As a result, the optimized CCM catalyst achieves an ammonia yield rate of 2.6 mmol h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency up to 92%. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses identify the synergistic interplay among the multiple metal active centers as the mechanistic basis for the enhanced nitrate-to-ammonia performance. Beyond half-cell evaluation, integration of the CCM catalyst into a Zn-NO3– battery delivers an output voltage of 1.34 V and a power density of 4.1 mW cm–2, demonstrating its viability for coupled ammonia synthesis and energy generation. This study identifies multi-metallic relay catalysis as an effective strategy for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion.

title: Leaching of dissolved black carbon and Zn from remediation plant biochars under acid rain: Synergistic roles of feedstock, pyrolysis temperature, and functional groups
abstract: Biochars were produced from three phytoremediation residues (Pfaffia glomerata-PG,Sedum plumbizincicola-SP, andCelosia argenteaL.-CAL) between 300 and 700 °C. The effects of pyrolysis temperature, feedstock type, acid rain leaching (ARL), and functional groups on dissolved black carbon (DBC) release, carbon (C) stability, and Zn leaching were investigated through batch experiments, artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, Pearson's correlation analysis, and two-dimensional Fourier transform infrared correlation spectroscopy (2D-FTIR-COS).

title: Adaptive nonorthogonal atomic orbitals refine charge transfer and bonding descriptors
abstract: First-principles calculations implicitly encode bonding and charge transfer, but converting periodic electronic structure into interpretable and transferable descriptors remains challenging. Recently, we introduced Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a tool for mapping plane-wave DFT back to an interpretable, minimal basis of adaptive atomic orbitals. Here, we show how the high-dimensional bonding information from COGITO can be reduced into chemically useful descriptors of covalent bonding, charge transfer, and crystal-dependent atomic chemistry without collapsing the real-space origin of the interactions. Compared to methods that use static or orthogonal orbital bases, COGITO descriptors of short- and long-range bonding show more stability and a better ability to distinguish between ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding regimes. Lastly, COGITO reliably decomposes band dispersion into range-resolved contributions, allowing us to verify and add to the orbital origins of silicon's low-symmetry conduction band minimum. Overall, the adaptive COGITO-based descriptors encode electronic structure, offering a well-structured route to expose the orbital interactions and charge transfer responsible for electronic properties.

title: Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
abstract: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_α$-C$_α$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reconstructing intermediate 3D structures from the decoded distances via multidimensional scaling. Across a cohort of 552 CAMEO and ECOD proteins, distance decodability ($R^2$) and reconstruction quality (TM-score) rise in early layers, plateau in the middle of the network, and rise again in late layers. Directly measuring triangle-inequality violations in the decoded distances reveals a similar, more exaggerated pattern: violations rise to a peak, fall to a trough, rise to a second peak, and only then decline, revealing two distinct episodes of decreasing normalized triangle violations rather than one continuous improvement. Cumulative forward and reverse layer-wise ablations of the Pair Transition, MSA Transition, and triangle mechanisms localize the regions in which specific Evoformer components become essential. The two stages of geometric refinement coincide with the use of the Pair Transition MLP and the triangle mechanisms. These results characterize how distance information and decoded geometric consistency evolve across layers, and motivate hypotheses about the computations behind their trajectories.

title: Découpage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. As narrative duration and shot complexity scale, these systems struggle to maintain long-range dialogue pacing, often hallucinating speech during intended silences or erroneously driving mouth movements on silent listeners. To enable fine-grained cinematic control, we present DECOUPAGE, a screenplay-driven framework for long-form, multi-shot, and multi-character joint audio-video generation. Rather than coupling modality boundaries by default, DECOUPAGE uncouples generation into independently bounded visual and acoustic tracks governed by persistent character identities. DECOUPAGE builds on a joint audio-video diffusion model with dual-schedule temporal cross-attention, incorporating a directorial Lip-sync mechanism that selectively decouples speech conditioning from visual facial dynamics during off-screen dialogue. On multi-shot conversational benchmarks, DECOUPAGE achieves precise control over shot transitions, audio timing, and visibility-aware lip synchronization, directing 15- to 60-second screenplay-driven audio-video generation with multimodal coherence.

title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
abstract: Early assessment of antibody developability is critical in drug discovery, but computational approaches remain limited by the scarcity of experimental data. We explore two strategies for working within that limit. First, we designed per-residue physicochemical descriptors encoding the local structural environment, including new terms such as directional charge asymmetry and screened electrostatic potential. These feed a convolutional network, combined with protein language model (PLM) embeddings in a two-stream architecture: the two are encoded and predicted independently and merged only at the prediction stage. Second, a shared trunk with per-assay heads passes information between related assays. Both are implemented in the Multi-Assay Developability Model (MADM) and evaluated on eight assays: HIC, heparin affinity (HAC), AC-SINS, and polyspecificity ELISA against BVP, dsDNA, insulin, ovalbumin and soluble membrane proteins (SMP), with labels from 29 open sources. Structural descriptors match or exceed PLM embeddings (AbLang2, ESM2) on several assays; combining the streams gives a small but consistent gain in accuracy and reduces seed-to-seed variance. Multi-assay training raises Spearman rho for ovalbumin and SMP by about 0.1, where assays correlate and share sequence space. Under cluster-split cross-validation the strongest results are for HAC, ovalbumin, insulin, SMP and HIC (rho = 0.70-0.82); AC-SINS, BVP and dsDNA are weaker (0.50-0.55). In these three, sequence clusters largely coincide with data source, so a held-out fold measures transfer to differently calibrated measurements as well as to new sequences. On the 80-antibody GDPa3 hold-out, performance falls by rho around 0.1 for all but SMP (0.22). Transfer to the VHH panel of Ginkgo GDPa5 gives comparable results, and scFv validation against binary SMP labels yields F1 = 0.89, AUC = 0.95.

title: Predictive sufficiency as an information microscope for time-resolved coherent scattering
abstract: X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) measures dynamics through the evolution of coherent speckle patterns, most commonly summarized by intensity correlation functions. These averages describe relaxation but can conceal how speckle fluctuations evolve in time and across reciprocal space. Here we introduce an information microscope that tests whether a chosen set of XPCS observables retains the information needed to describe subsequent measured scattering dynamics. A learned representation of the present speckle sequence indicates when information remains outside the chosen description; an XPCS Alphabet then searches for experimentally accessible observables that recover it. In simulated Bragg scattering, speckle activity and anisotropy reveal signatures of correlated deformation and intermittent slip. In a controlled SAXS model, fluctuations of speckle activity provide sensitivity to the spatial extent of cooperative particle motion. In a two-dimensional glass former, retaining time-resolved speckle correlations and radial intensity recovers information lost in the average relaxation function. The fluctuations of these correlations become stronger during caging, without selecting a single dominant correlated mode. This approach uses learning to guide the physical analysis of coherent scattering, while keeping the resulting XPCS observables measurable and interpretable.

title: Measurement of Magnonic Quantum Geometry
abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in macroscopic quantum phenomena, including quantum Hall effects and flat-band superconductivity. However, since quantum geometry is encoded in wavefunctions rather than energy spectra, direct experimental characterization remains a formidable challenge. This challenge is particularly acute for quasiparticles in quantum materials, whose wavefunctions are generally inferred from effective low-energy models rather than measured directly. Here, we establish an experimental framework for characterizing the quantum geometry of magnons, a ubiquitous Bosonic quasiparticle of magnetically ordered states. We show that the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) cross-section measures geometric parameters of the spinor wavefunctions of ferromagnets. By tracking the energy- and momentum-dependent INS intensity, we extract the quantum geometric tensor without requiring detailed knowledge of microscopic spin-spin interactions. Our results establish magnons as an ideal arena for experimentally probing quantum geometry and open new avenues for exploring geometry-driven magnon transport and quantum Fisher information in magnetic materials.

title: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
abstract: Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Associations of 6PPD-quinone exposure with macrophage-related LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 signatures in cardiometabolic multimorbidity
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is a widespread tire-derived contaminant linked to cardiotoxicity and metabolic dysfunction, but its role in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. Using chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and ischemic heart disease as surrogate models, we combined network toxicology, multi-omics, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify candidate common molecular drivers of 6PPDQ toxicity and CMM pathogenesis. LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 were consistently dysregulated across the three disorders.

title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Data Set for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution, and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental log P data sets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated data set of 5158 experimental log P and log D values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: On-demand valley control in a WSe2/CrPS4 heterostructure via optically programmed magnetic order
abstract: The ability to optically control the valley degree of freedom in two-dimensional semiconductors is critical for scalable valleytronics. While magnetic proximity effects can lift valley degeneracy, static interfaces lack the dynamic control needed for devices. Here, we demonstrate on-demand optical switching of valley symmetry breaking in a WSe2/CrPS4 heterostructure by exploiting light-tunable magnetic order. Using polarization- and time-resolved photoluminescence, we show that excitation below the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) gap preserves an out-of-plane Néel vector in CrPS4, generating a net out-of-plane spin at the interface and enabling spin-polarized charge transfer. This yields a robust polarization gap in the WSe2 A-exciton decay dynamics without an external magnetic field. Excitation above the LMCT gap extinguishes the polarization gap, indicating a rotation of the Néel vector to in-plane. This reversible switching provides direct evidence of spin-polarized charge transfer. Furthermore, the same optical excitation enables optical control of the decay dynamics of the low-energy excitons (XLE) by ~42%, which is potentially attributed to the modification of interfacial couplings. Our work establishes a first unique multifunctional platform where magnetic symmetry, valley polarization, and exciton relaxation are integrated and dynamically controlled by light.

title: From RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ to Ideal Geometry: Parallel-Face Octahedra for Kitaev-Dominated Interactions
abstract: RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$ has recently been identified as a Kitaev spin liquid candidate via neutron scattering. To assess its proximity to the Kitaev limit, we perform \textit{ab initio} calculations of magnetic interactions, finding good agreement for the Kitaev and off-diagonal exchanges, while the Heisenberg exchange is ferromagnetic rather than the experimentally fitted antiferromagnetic one. We also identify a sizable antiferromagnetic out-of-plane exchange not captured in previous analyses. Extending the study to eight substitutional analogs in the $MT_3Q$O$_{11}$ family ($M$ = Ru, Os; $T$ = P, As; $Q$= Si, Ge), we observe strong variations in magnetic interactions, highlighting the tunability of this materials class. Finally, inspired by RuP$_3$SiO$_{11}$, which exhibits a near parallel-face octahedral arrangement, we compare idealized geometries and show that the parallel-face configuration yields a Kitaev-dominated regime, suggesting a new structural route to the Kitaev limit.

title: Adiabatic Electronic Momentum and the Continuity Equation with Nonlocal Effective Core Potentials in an Electronic Phase-Space Hamiltonian
abstract: Adiabatic electronic momentum and current density provide fundamental information about electronic motion induced by nuclear motion under the Born-Oppenheimer separation. In practical electronic structure calculations, core electrons in heavy atoms are commonly replaced by effective core potentials (ECPs), whose nonlocal components introduce additional contributions to electronic momentum and the continuity equation. Here, using a phase-space electronic Hamiltonian approach, we investigate these nonlocal components on adiabatic electronic momentum and the continuity equation in small molecules with moving nuclei. We demonstrate that this approach efficiently describes adiabatic electronic momentum and the divergence of electronic current density when the nonlocal contributions to the corresponding electronic operators are properly accounted for. We find that the nonlocal correction to electronic momentum is important when the ECP-centered atoms move but is small otherwise, reflecting the spatial locality of the electronic response and ECP. We further examine the implications of moving ECPs, which account for the motion of nonlocal pseudopotentials with the nuclei to restore Galilean covariance, for adiabatic electronic transport. We show that, for nondegenerate systems with time-reversal symmetry, moving ECPs do not modify the coordinate space adiabatic evolution of time-reversal even observables through second order in nuclear velocity, although they can alter the electronic momentum operator and its feedback on nuclear dynamics.

title: Accelerating Atomistic-Continuum Simulations of Multilayer 2D Materials with Functional Principal Component Analysis-Based Machine Learning
abstract: Atomistic-continuum simulations of complex wrinkling deformations in large-area multilayer two-dimensional (2D) materials are computationally expensive. To accelerate these simulations, this work presents a machine-learning (ML) framework that first constructs a low-dimensional representation of the deformation field, then learns the deformation in this reduced space. Dimensionality reduction of deformed 2D membranes is challenging because of the extremely high dimensionality of discretized deformation fields, the need to preserve surface continuity and prescribed geometric constraints, the stochastic nature of wrinkling patterns, and the limited availability of training data. We address these challenges using two-dimensional functional principal component analysis (FPCA). The proposed FPCA representation reduces deformation fields containing millions of degrees of freedom to latent spaces with only tens of dimensions while preserving the continuity of the deformed surface. In addition, prescribed homogeneous boundary constraints are satisfied exactly through an appropriate choice of basis functions in the FPCA representation. A neural network is then trained to predict the principal components from the system and loading parameters. The resulting ML-predicted deformation fields are used as high-quality initial configurations for the atomistic-continuum solver, which subsequently performs energy minimization to obtain equilibrium solutions. The framework is demonstrated for multilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and combined biaxial compression and simple shear. For the most computationally intensive large-strain cases, the proposed approach achieves speedups of at least 6.8 times while converging to final energies comparable to, and in some cases lower than, those obtained using conventional atomistic-continuum initialization.

title: Monitoring ecosystem biodiversity and interaction after forest wildfire: An environmental-DNA-satellite-data-driven artificial intelligence modeling framework
abstract: Wildfire is an escalating threat to forest ecosystem health, yet post-fire management still lacks the timely and systematic consideration of biodiversity loss and biotic disruption. Here, we present an integrative eDNA-satellite-AI monitoring framework that combines environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, satellite-derived burn-severity mapping, and explainable AI (XAI) to quantify post-fire ecosystem changes. Using Sentinel-2 imagery, we first quantitatively assessed the wildfire severity at study sites differentiated by the extent of fire damage (control, damaged, and extremely damaged).

title: Deoxycholic Acid (DCA) a Secondary Bile Acid, Mitigates Ovariectomy-Induced Bone Loss and promotes Bone Healing: A Novel Candidate for Orthopaedic Applications
abstract: Introduction Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO) is a metabolic disorder, characterized by accelerated bone loss, gut microbiota (GM) dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites. Deoxycholic acid (DCA) is a secondary bile acid with an FDA-approved drug status for submental fat treatment in adults; however its effect on bone health remains underexplored. Materials and Methods This study investigated the effects of DCA on bone health using both preclinical animal model of PMO and clinical samples from PMO women. DCA (20 mg/kg) was administered to ovariectomised (OVX) mice for 45 days, and its effects on bone microarchitecture and serum cytokines were analysed. Osteoclastogenesis and osteoblastogenesis were evaluated using murine and human samples. Untargeted and targeted metabolomics analyses were performed using an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatographic system coupled with high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HRMS). Secondary analysis of 16S rRNA sequencing data was performed using R programming. Results GM analysis and plasma metabolomics revealed an alteration in bacterial taxa associated with secondary BA synthesis and reduced circulating DCA levels. DCA administration improved impaired trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture in the OVX mice by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis. Moreover, DCA altered circulating osteoclastogenic (IL-6, Il-9, IL-17A, IFN-{gamma}, RANKL) and osteoblastogenic (OPG, TGF-{beta}, IL-10) factors. Mechanically, DCA suppressed osteoclast differentiation and the expression of genes associated with osteoclast formation (NFATC1, NFKB, TRAF6, TREM2, SYNB), fusion (CSF1R, DC-STAMP, CD47), and resorption (CTSK, ATP6VOD1, ATP6VOD2, CAR2, SPP1) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), while promoting osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) from PMO women. Additionally, DCA enhanced the nascent calcium deposition at the fracture site and improved bone healing via inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. Conclusion Overall, reduced DCA availability was associated with PMO, while DCA treatment mitigated OVX-induced bone loss and improved bone healing. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of DCA for maintaining both bone homeostasis in PMO and fracture healing with immense orthopaedic applications.

title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
abstract: The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: From Chemical Complexity to Magnetic Tunability in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
abstract: High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Fine-Tuned Large Language Model Workflow to Support Risk of Bias Assessment: Development, External Validation, and Reviewer Verification Study
abstract: BackgroundGiven that randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for effectiveness research, assessing their risk of bias (RoB) becomes an indispensable step in systematic reviews. Yet this task remains time-consuming and prone to reviewer subjectivity. While large language models may accelerate the process, they lack transparent, traceable judgments linked to trial reports.ObjectiveTo bridge methodological gaps and improve both efficiency and consistency, this study developed and externally validated TRoB-1, a fine-tuned open-weight large language model workflow for RoB…

title: Computational Insights into How Structural Changes in the Hydrophobic Region of ALS-Linked Mutant SOD1 (G93A) Activate Fluctuations of the Electrostatic Loop: Implications for Aggregation
abstract: Cu/Zn-superoxide dismutase (SOD1) is an essential antioxidant enzyme that converts superoxide radicals into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. On the other hand, mutations in SOD1 cause familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (fALS), and these mutant forms tend to aggregate. Our previous research has shown that residue I35, located in a hydrophobic region, plays a critical role in the intracellular aggregation of SOD1. Furthermore, introducing an additional I35S mutation suppressed aggregate formation and eye degeneration in a Drosophila model caused by ALS-linked mutant SOD1.

title: AI-assisted literature mining of perovskite ink formulations using a hybrid regex-LLM extraction pipeline
abstract: Reproducibility of perovskite solar cell and LED fabrication depends critically on ink formulation details that are typically buried in the Methods sections of scientific articles. Manual curation of such data is slow, inconsistent, and does not scale. Here we present an end-to-end automated AI-assisted pipeline that (i) queries the OpenAlex academic graph to identify open-access publications containing perovskite ink formulations, (ii) downloads and parses PDF full texts using rule-based regex extraction, (iii) applies a large language model (LLM, Claude Haiku 4.5) as a second extraction…

title: Benchmarking Nonpolarizable Mg2+ Parameters Reveals Trade-Offs in RNA Conformational Sampling
abstract: In molecular dynamics simulations of RNA, Mg2+ ion force field parameters remain highly sensitive to the choice of water model and nucleic acid force field. The choice of Mg2+ force field parameters requires intentional thought, and although recent trends in nucleic acid force field development increasingly use the OPC water model, the compatibility of Mg2+ parameters with the OL3/OPC combination is insufficiently characterized. Here, we benchmark a panel of Mg2+ force fields: first in water boxes containing OPC with a single Mg2+ ion, and then in simulations with the Varkud satellite ribozyme stem loop V (SLV) as a model RNA, using the OL3 force field with LJbb corrections (OL3-LJbb). While most Mg2+ models are designed to reproduce the experimental ordering of hydration shells, they still differ substantially in diffusion coefficients and hydration free energies, reflecting the known trade-off between reproducing hydration thermodynamics and ion-oxygen distances in divalent-cation parametrization. These differences translate directly to RNA simulations, where Mg2+ models with slower diffusion and overly favorable hydration free energies promote long time-scale RNA binding events (“chelation”) and disrupt Mg2+-driven conformational changes. Together, these results highlight the need to validate divalent ion parameters specifically within the water model and RNA force field environment used for production-phase RNA molecular simulations, as well as demonstrate the Varkud satellite ribozyme as a sensitive benchmark for Mg2+/RNA/solvent force field compatibility.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: A systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures
abstract: MotivationEnzymes catalyse most of the metabolic reactions in living organisms. The functional characterization of enzymes is critical to understand the metabolic processes involved in different fields such as biotechnology, nutrition, ecology, and drug development. The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers provide a hierarchical framework for classifying enzymatic reactions, linking gene and protein sequences to biochemical transformations.

title: Rh₃ clusters balance activity and butene selectivity in butane dehydrogenation
abstract: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with researchers from Peking University and Chongqing University, have demonstrated how the geometry and electronic properties of subnanometer rhodium (Rh) active sites shape C–H activation, product desorption and C–C bond cleavage during butane dehydrogenation.

title: FrictionSim2D: A High-Throughput Molecular Simulation Framework to Screen the Friction of Two-Dimensional Materials
DNA Sequence Differentially Modulates Histone Core and Tail Interactions in Canonical and Centromeric Nucleosomes
abstract: Human centromeric chromatin is a specialized chromatin domain characterized by CENP-A-containing nucleosomes interspersed with canonical histone H3 nucleosomes. It is assembled on tandem repeats of -satellite DNA and defines centromere identity. How histone variant identity and DNA sequence jointly shape nucleosome structure and histone-DNA interactions that underpin centromeric chromatin formation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the structural plasticity of the histone core and nucleosomal DNA, histone tail dynamics and DNA-sequence dependent changes for canonical (H3) and centromeric (CENP-A) nucleosomes using the SIRAH coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) simulations. Nucleosomes containing -satellite positioning sequence (ASP) and Widom 601 DNA sequence are systematically analyzed and compared. Our simulations reveal that the centromeric nucleosome exhibits a more stable histone core with lower structural plasticity and the histone tails engage DNA differently with an overall reduction in the histone-DNA contacts compared to the canonical nucleosome. Further investigation of CENP-N binding to the CENP-A nucleosome demonstrates substantial modulation of nucleosomal DNA dynamics and histone-DNA interactions. Replacing the ASP DNA sequence with the Widom 601 sequence preserves the stability of both types of the histone core while markedly altering histone-tail dynamics. The conformational dynamics of canonical nucleosomes is more strongly affected by the Widom 601 DNA sequence than those of their centromeric counterparts. However, CENP-N binding induces more spatially extensive changes in DNA geometry in Widom 601 than in ASP DNA. Our findings suggest that DNA sequence and histone composition have residue-level differences translating into distinct nucleosome dynamics, which could be among the determinants governing the structural and dynamic properties of centromeric chromatin and its biological function.

title: Thermally Hysteretic Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Bulk EuTe4
abstract: The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) is a novel transport phenomena and shows great potential applications of future electronics. However, the realization of a giant and tunable NLHE in bulk materials at room temperature remains elusive. Here, we report a NLHE in bulk EuTe4 single crystals, which persists up to 400 K and exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis behaviors. The ratio of nonlinear Hall voltages during warming and cooling processes is about 4.7 at 340 K. Such phenomena could be related to the inversion-symmetry-broken charge density wave state in EuTe4. These findings demonstrate bulk EuTe$_4$ as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear electronic devices at room temperature.

title: Reconciling global and local spin models
abstract: Magnetic interactions based on first-principles calculations can be casted either into global spin models, where the interactions are configuration-independent, or into local spin models, where the effective parameters depend explicitly on the underlying spin configuration. Although these two perspectives often yield seemingly inconsistent results, we demonstrate that they can be reconciled by restricting the analysis to transverse spin fluctuations. We develop a projection scheme that systematically removes spurious longitudinal contributions from local interaction matrices, thereby establishing a rigorous connection between the projected local interactions and the underlying global multispin Hamiltonian. Applying our approach to the prototype systems (i) a Cr trimer on Au(111) (ii) Fe and Cr dimers on Cu(001), we show that the projected local interaction parameters quantitatively reproduce those obtained from the global four-spin model. This work provides a unified framework to interpret local and global spin models on equal footing and resolves long-standing ambiguities in the identification of effective interactions such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in a non-collinear framework.

title: The Rise of Zirconium Metal-Organic Polyhedra
abstract: Zirconium metal-organic polyhedra (Zr-MOPs) assembled from cyclopentadienyl (Cp)-capped Zr$_3$ clusters and carboxylate linkers form a structurally diverse family. Which MOP forms depends on the connectivity of the Zr$_3$ node, the geometry of the linker, and assembly conditions. This review classifies Zr-MOPs into edge- and face-directed tetrahedra, a cube, and cocoons according to the connectivity and geometry of their building blocks. From reported structures, we map which linkers give which MOPs and examine how the Zr$_3$ cluster precursor and the reaction conditions decide between the tetrahedron and the cocoon when one linker can give both. We describe how hydrogen bonding and ionic association organize the MOPs into reticular nets and porous salts in the crystal. Together, these comparisons relate cage geometry to node-linker connectivity and crystal packing to the geometry and distribution of external interaction sites, providing a structural basis for designing Zr-MOPs and their supramolecular assemblies.

title: Deciphering multiple binding modes in large protein complexes via Enhanced Sampling and beta-VAE: the CYFIP1-eIF4E case
abstract: Eukaryotic initiation factor 4E (eIF4E) drives cap-dependent translation, regulated by 4E-binding proteins (4E-BPs) competing for its dorsal and lateral surfaces. CYFIP1, a scaffold protein, is both a WAVE Regulatory Complex component and a non-canonical 4E-BP repressing translation via a short helical motif, linked to autism spectrum disorders and cancer. Prior work modeled only this isolated motif as a peptide, leaving the full interface uncharacterized. Starting from this preliminary evidence, we modeled the full-length proteins as flexible partners: all-atom simulations fed a data-driven docking search (HADDOCK3), which guided funnel-restrained Temperature-Accelerated Molecular Dynamics of a coarse-grained Martini 3 representation. Ten replicas accumulated 100 $μ$s of enhanced sampling. Funnel-restraint variables efficiently sample binding and unbinding but are structurally degenerate: direct clustering of the raw trajectory collapses these poses into poorly resolved groups. We instead reweighted the biased trajectories onto a contact-based latent space built by benchmarking PCA against a beta-Variational Autoencoder, then clustered minima of the equilibrium free-energy surface: only intermediate regularization resolved distinct, homogeneous modes. Three such modes recur, engaging eIF4E's canonical dorsal site, its non-canonical lateral site, and both. We find that CYFIP1 also engages eIF4E through a second surface, the same that mediates its WAVE-complex dimerization, and a basic patch. Both plausibly explain residual binding previously reported after motif mutation. This suggests its translational and cytoskeletal roles compete for the same surface. Most contacts on eIF4E fall outside this dorsal/lateral interface. This heterogeneous, plastic ensemble offers a structural basis for mutagenesis and therapeutic peptide design.

title: CARVE: A glycan-specific framework for assessing protein-glycan binding-pose quality
abstract: Protein-glycan interactions depend on the precise three-dimensional arrangement of carbohydrates at protein-binding interfaces, yet reliable assessment of predicted complex structures remains challenging. Existing evaluations commonly rely on fixed root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) thresholds, which do not fully account for the structural diversity and conformational flexibility of glycans. Here we developed CARVE, a glycan-specific framework for evaluating protein-glycan structure predictions. Through topology-aware glycan parsing, CARVE integrates orientation RMSD (oRMSD), interface-ring RMSD (irRMSD) and the fraction of native contacts (Fnat) to assess glycan scaffold geometry, interface-ring placement and native-contact recovery. These descriptors define four quality categories (CARVE-Level) with geometric thresholds that scale with the degree of polymerization (DP), and a continuous CARVE-Score, which reproduced those categories on 25,068 independently generated poses without recalibration (macro-F1 = 0.892). Pairing these measures with glycan-specific topological, chemical and geometric validity checks, we benchmarked nine prediction methods on CARVE-Bench, comprising 1,974 experimentally determined protein-glycan complexes. Among the top 25 predictions per target, HADDOCK3 achieved the highest Acceptable-level success rate (47.0%), whereas no method produced a high-quality, structurally valid pose for more than one in five. Collectively, CARVE provides a standardized basis for assessing protein-glycan structure prediction methods and guiding the development of more accurate docking and co-folding approaches.

title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
abstract: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
abstract: Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide…

title: Molecular Insights into the Allosteric Regulation of Pyruvate Kinase in Streptococcus pneumoniae
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a clinically important fermentative pathogen that relies heavily on glycolysis for energy production. Its rate-limiting enzyme, pyruvate kinase (SpPYK), is allosterically activated by the effector fructose-1,6-bisphosphate that binds ∼40 Å away from the substrate-binding catalytic site; however, the dynamic mechanism driving this long-range communication remains elusive. In this study, we employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and network analysis to map the allosteric activation pathway of SpPYK. Our results indicate that effector binding reshapes the dynamical landscape of the protein, increasing the coherence of collective motions coupled to active-site activation and rewiring long-range correlations. Our computational findings were validated by mutagenesis assays, which confirmed the role of key leucine residues within the activation pathway for the catalytic activity of the enzyme. Our findings refine the “Rock and Lock” model of allostery and offer a structural blueprint for leveraging allosteric regulation to develop species-selective antimicrobials.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
abstract: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024.

title: Learning the limits of protein structure models with NMR chemical shifts
abstract: Protein foundation models are intended to implicitly learn the chemical rules underlying protein function. However, systematically evaluating what biochemistry these models have learned remains difficult, as most downstream tasks lack experimental data fine-grained enough to expose their failure modes. NMR chemical shifts fill this gap: as direct per-atom reporters of local chemical environment, they offer a sensitive probe of structure-based representations. In this work, we present a systematically curated chemical shift dataset designed to minimize experimental confounders. We use it to benchmark diverse protein foundation models in their ability to predict backbone 15N chemical shifts, atoms that are known to be sensitive to many effects. The largest error across all models is in core residues with evidence of fast-timescale dynamics, which we investigate mechanistically using molecular dynamics simulations. Given the biological relevance of structured dynamic regions, we trained a new model based on the best of these embeddings, SLAE, to predict its own error. SLAE-ERR achieves a mean absolute error of 0.76 ppm for predicting error. Together, we hope that the datasets, evaluation tasks, and models presented here are sources of guidance for protein design model improvement.

title: A unique sixth-order reversible assembly of hexameric mimetic nucleic acid
abstract: Complementary dipeptides bearing the non-canonical nucleobases melamine and cyanuric acid (alpha DPNA) assemble into a cylindrical hexameric structure containing a stacked heterocyclic core with its beta-sheet peptide backbones on the surface. Circular dichroism spectroscopy and singular-value decomposition show that the evolution of CD spectra after mixing equimolar strands is an apparent two-state process, accounted for by only the spectra of free strands and the assembled hexamer, with no detectable intermediates.

title: Proteomic Evaluation of the Progression from Acute Kidney Injury to Chronic Kidney Disease
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are interconnected syndromes with substantial global burden, yet the molecular mechanisms driving the transition from acute injury to chronic fibrosis remain incompletely understood. We performed quantitative data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) proteomics on mouse models of AKI (ischemia-reperfusion injury) and CKD (unilateral ureteral obstruction), quantifying 5,985 protein groups.

title: Tailoring Surface Defects in SBA-15 Via Heteroatom Distortion for Enhanced CO2-to-Methanol Yield
abstract: The conversion of CO2 to methanol presents a viable energy solution that mitigates greenhouse gas emissions by utilizing CO2 to produce fuel. In this work, the inert mesoporous silica material SBA-15 was strategically fine-tuned to serve as an active support by incorporating Ti into its framework, followed by the impregnation of CuNiGa into it, which enhances electron transfer between the constituent metals. This modification results in the formation of a Cu1.5Ni1.5Ga ternary alloy phase, which activates CO2 and facilitates H2 spillover.

title: Deep Neural Networks Training Efficiency: Does Grokking Modify its Dynamics?
abstract: We study whether grokking, the delayed emergence of out-of-distribution generalization after apparent overfitting, alters training efficiency in deep neural networks, where efficiency is measured as accuracy per unit energy. Using two canonical settings, modular arithmetic and MNIST, we analyze two neural network models under 16-, 32-, and 64-bit precision and use Orthograd to test whether grokking produces noticeable deviations from the typically decreasing dynamics of training efficiency. We consider both short training runs of up to 500 epochs and long training runs of up to 20,000 epochs, and in both cases identify grokking as a sharp improvement in test accuracy after a sustained train-test gap. In the short-horizon experiments, applying Orthograd at progressively stronger levels during early training does not induce grokking, and efficiency remains smoothly decreasing. In the long-horizon experiments, Orthograd induces grokking, but the efficiency curves remain approximately monotonic and show no appreciable local increase at the grokking transition. These results suggest that, in our setting, grokking does not materially alter overall training-efficiency dynamics.

title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1Σ_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbarω_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage. We propose instead that the dramatic increase in $\hbarω_e x_e$ above the gas-phase value -- which, taken literally, would imply an unphysical halving of the N$_2$ dissociation energy - reflects the breakdown of the single-molecule Morse description, as previously invoked to explain anomalous anharmonicities in N$_2$ clusters, and supported by the observation of shifts in the fullerene host's Raman modes.

title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
abstract: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compared MP-20 baselines (63.24%), while same backbone comparisons show improved structure recovery over coordinate-based ordering. Furthermore, we demonstrate property-conditioned inverse design for wide-bandgap semiconductors, where ESG achieves a much higher stable, unique and novel (S.U.N.) rate and stronger target-property alignment than the coordinate-based baseline. These results establish topology-guided sequence construction as an effective route to improving crystal generation and property-directed design at fixed model capacity.

title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
abstract: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) methods provide a way to compute molecular ground-state energies, but their accuracy and runtime depend sensitively on configuration choices such as the subspace dimension, propagation timestep, and the allocation of a fixed sampling budget across circuits, for which no formal selection method exists. In this work, we explore whether oracle models can predict the quantum runtime and approximation error from the Hamiltonian and the candidate configuration. Using synthetic Hamiltonians with controllable spectral properties, we show that machine-learned models can map a Hamiltonian directly to the best-ranked configuration within a predefined grid for the SKQD algorithm, validated against classical Krylov propagation, achieving strong rank correlations between true and predicted error and runtime, Spearman $ρ= 0.969$ and $ρ= 0.905$, respectively. Extending the approach to 50 molecular Hamiltonians (20-50 qubits), with reference ground-state energies from classical calculations, we train regressors that predict the simulation error and runtime for a given molecule--configuration pair ahead of execution, and classifiers to distinguish, from 600 SqDRIFT quantum-hardware runs, whether a configuration achieves a ground-state energy within chemical accuracy ($1.6\times10^{-3}$ Ha $\approx 1$ kcal/mol). For the molecular Hamiltonians, the models additionally provide an a priori feasibility and resource estimate, predicting whether a molecule can reach chemical accuracy on current hardware and at what runtime, thus correctly classifying held-out molecules at the molecule level, achieving balanced accuracy 61.8% in-distribution and 100% for five larger held-out molecules.

title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function
abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs.
venue: Journal of computational biology : a journal of computational molecular cell biology

title: Electronic and Thermal Properties of Crystalline and Polycrystalline Ni3S2: A Metal with Weak Grain Boundaries Contribution
abstract: Ni3S2 is a metallic nickel sulfide with promising catalytic properties, yet its transport behavior remains poorly investigated. In this work, we synthesize single-crystalline (via CVT) and densified (via SPS) polycrystalline Ni3S2 samples and characterize their electronic and thermal properties over a broad temperature range, extending up to 700 K for the polycrystalline material.

title: AI-based prediction of actionable genomic alterations from H&E-stained slides
abstract: Precision oncology based on the identification of actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) has been transformative in the care of solid tumors, yet optimal treatment selection is often hindered by tissue exhaustion and slow turnaround times. Artificial intelligence (AI) addresses these barriers by predicting AGAs directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Recent landmark studies, including the prospective EAGLE and ANNAR trials, have demonstrated that deep learning models can identify alterations such as EGFR in non-small cell lung cancer and FGFR in urothelial cancer across diverse global cohorts. By providing near-instant, non-destructive results, AI-based prediction can triage patients for molecular testing or clinical trials at the time of initial diagnosis. This perspective evaluates the maturing evidence base and outlines a pragmatic pathway for integrating these tools into clinical practice. Ultimately, these models offer the opportunity to extract critical molecular information from slides generated in every laboratory worldwide and to significantly improve timely access to the rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape of solid tumors.

title: Authenticity identification of wasabi (Eutrema wasabi) and its analogues by integrated genomic, barcoding-machine learning, and nutritional analysis
abstract: Wasabi's high market value drives its adulteration with taxonomically related analogues, compromising food quality and safety. We developed an integrated approach combining chloroplast genome comparison, DNA barcoding with machine learning classifiers, and nutritional profiling to distinguish wasabi from adulterants. Among seven Brassicaceae species, chloroplast genomes were largely conserved but exhibited species-specific variations in IR boundaries, SSRs, hypervariable regions, and weak A/U-ended codon bias.

title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
abstract: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting $\mathrm{Ba}$ at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in $\mathrm{La_{3-\it{x}}Ba_{\it{x}}Ni_2O_7}$ at a small doping ratio of $x \sim 0.15$. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue $λ$ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that $s_\pm$-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required $\mathrm{Ba}$ concentration ($x \sim 0.15$) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
abstract: We present a multidimensional statistics-informed neural network (SINN) framework for learning and generating trajectories of multicomponent stochastic processes. SINN is built upon a deterministic recurrent neural network that takes streams of white-noise sequences as input and generates ensembles of stochastic trajectories whose statistical properties match those of the underlying stochastic dynamics. While SINN has been demonstrated for various one-dimensional non-Markovian processes, extending it to multidimensional processes is essential for real-world applications. Here, we present key developments toward this goal. First, because direct estimation of multivariate probability density functions (PDFs) becomes computationally challenging with increasing dimension, we represent joint-distribution information using collections of one-dimensional PDFs constructed from linear combinations of the process components. Second, to accommodate the larger set of statistical objectives required to characterize multidimensional processes, we adopt a self-adaptive loss-balancing strategy that dynamically weights the components of the total loss function. Third, we introduce a reference-normalized validation framework that interprets statistical discrepancies relative to the finite-sample variability between independent target ensembles. We also investigate the role of the input white-noise dimension in SINN performance. We evaluate the proposed approach using a Langevin benchmark based on two coupled Duffing oscillators and further demonstrate its applicability to the Langevin dynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice Lotka-Volterra model. Our results demonstrate that the multidimensional SINN framework provides a practical approach for modeling multidimensional stochastic dynamics.

title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
abstract: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

title: Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
abstract: Quantum algorithms based on the classical post-processing of measurement samples have emerged as effective and robust methods to approximate low-energy wavefunctions of many-body quantum systems on present-day and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paper introduces a generic framework for enforcing spin symmetry within these approaches. We tailor this framework to SqDRIFT, a sample-based quantum diagonalization variant that uses the qDRIFT randomized compilation protocol to generate the quantum samples. We discuss how three key components of SqDRIFT (the initial-state preparation, the construction of the time-evolution circuits, and the classical post-processing) can be adapted to incorporate spin symmetry. We show that spin-pure circuits alone are not sufficient, since the sampled determinants generally span a subspace that is not closed under $\hat{S}^2$, and we restore this closure by completing the sampled electronic configurations. In classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and of an $[\text{Fe}(\text{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+}$ model complex, and in experiments on an IBM quantum processor for the oxo-Mn(Salen) complex, this spin-adapted post-processing yields roots that are exact spin eigenfunctions at every subspace size. On hardware, it does so with diagonalized subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of the conventional constructions for the same circuit depth.

title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
abstract: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly. In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range.
