Theoretically, it leverages the synergistic effect of separation capabilities across both dimensions to substantially enhance peak capacity, providing robust technical support for analyzing complex systems such as traditional Chinese medicine. However, after nearly a decade of development and application, substantial gaps remain between its theoretical advantages and practical performance in TCM analysis.

title: Tautomerism and Diradical Character: Chemical and Electronic Structure of a High-Performance Organic Electrode Material
abstract: Bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) is a high-performance organic electrode material whose molecular structure remains a subject of debate, which we address in this joint experimentaltheoretical study. Using density functional theory (DFT) across multiple scales, from isolated molecules to periodic crystal structures, this work provides an atomistic insight into the structural and electronic complexity of TAQ.

title: Gain, Retention, or Loss of Aromaticity upon Surface Adsorption: π-Electron Systems on Cu(111)
abstract: Understanding the interactions between metal surfaces and the π-electron systems of flat-lying polycyclic conjugated hydrocarbons is central to designing metal–organic interfaces and on-surface synthesis. This surface interaction is sometimes rationalized in terms of aromaticity, which is usually evaluated for gas phase model systems and rarely for adsorbed molecules. Here, we use density functional theory to study changes in geometric and electronic aromaticity for 22 π-electron systems upon adsorption on Cu(111), from physisorption to strong chemisorption.

title: Bayesian Optimization Outperforms Experts for Spectral Model Development
abstract: Indirect Hard Modeling (IHM) is a physically motivated approach for quantitative spectral analysis that can account for nonlinear spectral changes, provides loweffort calibration, and allows extrapolation. However, realizing the full potential of IHM requires careful adjustment of model parameters and spectral preprocessing settings, which is typically performed manually and relies on expert knowledge. To address this limitation, we investigate Bayesian Optimization (BO) as a strategy for efficient IHM parameter tuning with mixed continuous, discrete, and categorical parameter spaces.

title: Donor priming and conformational control in arginine N-rhamnosylation by the glycosyltransferase EarP
abstract: EarP is an unusual glycosyltransferase that rhamnosylates R32 of bacterial elongation factor P (EF-P), catalyzing glycosylation of a poorly nucleophilic guanidinium moiety. How donor and acceptor are organized to enable this rare reaction remains incompletely understood. Here, we report the synthesis and use of complementary low-reactivity analogs of dTDP-rhamnose (dTDP-Rha) to capture structural states associated with substrate recognition and turnover by EarP from Neisseria meningitidis, supported by biochemical assays of glycosyl transfer.

title: synthmc: a precedent-based synthesizability score for transition metal complexes
abstract: Data-driven methods are increasingly being used for the in silico discovery of transition metal complexes (TMCs), ranging from machine learning models for high-throughput screening and generative models proposing new candidates to evolutionary algorithms for their de novo design. However, computationally discovered or designed TMCs are only rarely realized experimentally, in part because their synthesis is difficult and often not considered during the design process.

title: A mechanistic insight into the role of triplet states in excited-state deactivation of dibenzothiophene: a new fate for green chemistry
abstract: The environmental impact of petroleum derivatives is a current threat which needs to be studied and tackled in the present and near future. In this context, obtaining new insight about the degradation and remediation possibilities of polyaromatic sulphur heterocycles, and particularly dibenzothiophene, is a challenge requiring the full attention of the academic community. Thus, we have studied the dibenzothiophene excited state decay from a theoretical perspective, resorting to multiconfigurational methods, in order to obtain a full photophysical picture which until now was incomplete.

title: Linear-time Shape Alignment with ROSHAMBO3
abstract: Three-dimensional (shape) similarity is a useful primitive for virtual screening and molecular machine learning, but current open implementations are limited in performance by a quadratic inner loop across pairs of query-and databasemolecule atoms. ROSHAMBO3 achieves a 78–154× speedup over the previous open SOTA ROSHAMBO2 by using query-amortized Gaussian fields that make the inner loop linear combined with system-scale optimization at the algorithmic, GPU, and host layers, screening up to 55M query–conformer pairs/s on NVIDIA GPUs, with secondary CPU (x86, ARM) and Apple Metal backends.

title: Two-Step Recovery Kinetics with Distinct Time Scales in Stress-Softened Polyacrylamide-Carbon Nanotube Composite Hydrogels
abstract: Polyacrylamide-carbon nanotube (PAAm-CNT) composite hydrogels exhibit pronounced stress-softening alongside substantial CNT-induced toughening. Although stress-softening causes the reloading stress to drop significantly below the virgin loading stress, the underlying internal damage recovers given a sufficient resting period. We quantify the recovery dynamics using two independent metrics: the residual internal damage D R (defined as the hysteresis work loss) and the post-unloading residual strain ε R .

title: Ruthenium Catalyzed Reduction of N 2 O using MeOH as Hydrogen Source
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) is a significant contributor to climate change owing to its dual role as greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting molecule. Herein, the catalytic reduction of N 2 O to N 2 using methanol (MeOH) as a terminal reductant was investigated employing a series of Ru complexes supported by proton-responsive picoline- and lutidine-derived pincer ligands incorporating N-heterocyclic carbene donors (CNC and CNN).

title: Predicting the Fourth Analogue: Learning Stereochemical Transfer in Cyclic-Peptide Permeability
abstract: Combining stereochemical edits offers a direct way to explore cyclic-peptide chemical space. Once a reference peptide and two single-edit analogues have been measured, the modeling question is how molecular structure improves prediction beyond those three observations. We define this conditional permeability task using 1,154 chemically certified squares from four publications and evaluate transfer across 22 complete chemical families.

title: Metal-Free Spin Crossover Through Nitrogen-Intercalated Graphene Under Pressure
abstract: Spin crossover (SCO) phenomena, in which the spin state of an atom changes due to an external stimulus, have been the subject of ongoing research interest to this day. However, the considered atoms have been limited to transition metals like iron or cobalt. In this theoretical study, we show for the first time that external pressure can cause a nitrogen atom, i.e., a non-metal, to transit from a high spin (HS) to a low spin (LS) configuration.

title: AutoSPS-D2B: Automated Solid-Phase Synthesis Expands the Reaction Scope for Direct-to-Biology Libraries
abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) has emerged as a powerful accelerant in early drug discovery, bypassing compound purification to compress the design-make-test-analyse (DMTA) cycle. However, the chemistry underpinning D2B libraries is limited to just a few sequential transformations using assay-compatible reagents and solvents. By contrast, solid-phase synthesis (SPS) empowers a far broader range of reactions and is highly amenable to multistep synthesis, yet its potential as a source for D2B libraries remains largely underexplored.

title: Programmable Self-Sorting in Multi-Component Coordination Cage Systems via Ligand Tethering
abstract: Control over self-sorting in multi-component metal-organic self-assembly remains a major challenge as mixtures of ligands commonly yield statistical distributions of products. Integrative and heteromeric completive self-sorting regimes are both attractive non-statistical outcomes, but each typically requires system-specific design; switching between the two cannot readily be achieved within a single ligand set. Here, we show that a simple tethering strategy enables programmable self-sorting in heteroleptic Pd(II) coordination cages by chelation.

title: Microplastic Identification by Temperature-Resolved Fluorescence Imaging
abstract: Heating Nile Red-stained microplastics on a filter while imaging their fluorescence allows to determine their flowthrough temperatures, associated with melting or softening of the polymers. Using a widefield microscope and a consumer-grade camera we classify HDPE, LDPE, PP, PVC and PMMA by RGB values and flow-through temperature.

title: Structure Before Sequence: Physicochemical Catalytic Organization and Biological Reconstruction
abstract: Biological catalysis depends on highly organized protein and RNA architectures whose reproducible construction is itself sequence-supported, creating a familiar circularity in discussions of catalytic origins. This Perspective separates two questions that are often treated together: what physical organization is sufficient for catalytic function, and what sequencesupported biology adds to make selected catalytic architectures reproducibly reconstructable.

title: Light-induced signal enhancement in 13C solid-state NMR occurring in a flavin-tyrosine radical pair
abstract: “Light-oxygen-voltage” (LOV) domains are widespread flavin-containing proteins known for their numerous photosensory functions. Under illumination, some LOV domains form spin-correlated radical pairs (SCRPs), in which coherent spin evolution can lead to the buildup of transient nuclear hyperpolarization. In LOV domains, this solid-state photo-CIDNP (photochemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization) effect has so far been observed only with tryptophan as the electron donor. Here, we show that the effect can also be achieved with a tyrosine.

title: Complete Top-down Sequencing of Therapeutic Phosphorodiamidate Morpholino Oligomers by Multimodal Ion Activation in Both Polarities
abstract: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMOs) are an important class of approved antisense therapeutics whose neutral backbone presents significant challenges for tandem mass spectrometric sequencing. Here, we evaluate multiple ion activation strategies on a timsOmni™ prototype in both electrospray polarities using the approved PMO drugs viltolarsen (21-mer) and eteplirsen (30-mer).

title: A fluorescence polarization probe for rapid and quantitative analysis of interactions between Rubisco and small molecules
Physical consistency and completeness in the data-driven modeling of microwave absorbing materials
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been applied to the modeling of microwave absorbing materials, including the prediction of electromagnetic parameters and reflection loss (RL), yet the physical consistency of such models is rarely examined. This paper addresses two types of physical consistency problems in data-driven modeling: the physical inconsistency of predicted outputs and the physical incompleteness of input features. On the output side, we constructed a numerical integrator based on the Kramers-Kronig (KK) relation to test permittivity spectra output by ML models.

title: Machine learning-guided discovery and preliminary biological evaluation of novel GSK-3β inhibitory scaffolds with anti-inflammatory potential
abstract: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β) is a multifunctional serine/threonine kinase implicated in neurodegeneration, cancer, metabolic disorders, and inflammatory diseases. The discovery of structurally novel GSK-3β inhibitors remains important for developing new chemical probes and therapeutic starting points. In this study, we established a machine learning-assisted computational screening workflow for the identification of potential GSK-3β inhibitors.

title: CadreAI: Agentic AI for Semantically Decoupled Protein–Drug Design and Optimization
abstract: De novo drug design must balance global drug properties with local structural determinants of target specificity. However, existing methods often reduce both objectives to local geometric optimization, relying on blind, reward-driven perturbations that can disrupt essential scaffolds and compromise overall drug-likeness. To resolve this destructive optimization trap, we propose CadreAI, a semantically decoupled agentic de novo drug design framework. CadreAI explicitly decomposes the entire drug design process into two independent subtasks: target-oriented semantic planning and plan-conditioned molecular generation. This strict separation mitigates potential task interference, allowing each module to focus exclusively on its dedicated objective without mutual disruption. Crucially, the strategic logic of how to formulate these target-oriented plans is driven by Simulation-Guided Insight Consolidation (SGIC). To eliminate trial-and-error guessing, this persistent memory mechanism translates transient numerical docking feedback into reusable textual heuristics, allowing the agent to continuously learn and logically deduce subsequent structural edits. Evaluated on the CrossDocked2020 and DrugGen benchmarks, molecules generated by CadreAI achieve superior docking performance with suitable drug-likeness and synthetic accessibility. Additional Boltz-2 evaluations provide orthogonal computational validation of predicted structural plausibility and binding affinity. These results demonstrate that semantically decoupled reasoning offers a highly controllable and practical route for in silico therapeutic design.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: General Collaborative Intelligence: Architecting Cognition for Resilient Multi-Agent Ecosystems
abstract: Multi-agent unmanned systems are moving from isolated, ego-centric sensing toward collaborative intelligence, in which distributed agents exchange compact features to overcome a local observation trap that no single agent can escape: occlusions, finite sensor range, and environmental degradation. The field has matured across architectural, communication, embodied, resilience, and trust dimensions, yet existing surveys examine these dimensions in isolation and rarely expose the dependencies among them. This review offers a unified synthesis through 2 complementary lenses.

title: Ion-Dipole Engineered Hierarchical Ion-Gradient Piezoionic Elastomers for Enhanced Soft Energy Harvesting and Multimodal Sensing
abstract: Piezoionic elastomers transduce mechanical deformation into electrical signals through ion migration, yet achieving effective and stable ion gradient remains challenging. Here, we present hierarchical ion-gradient piezoionic elastomers (HiGPiE), featuring spherulitic ionic microcompartments coupled with nanoscale asymmetric ion organization and ion-polymer interactions within an [EMIM]+[BF4]-ionic liquid (IL)-incorporated PVDF matrix.

title: Epitaxial integration of GaN $μ$-platelets and thin films on metallic TiN using a hybrid approach
abstract: We demonstrate the synthesis of epitaxial, self-organized GaN $μ$-platelets on metallic TiN thin films. To this end, we first nucleate self-assembled GaN nanowires with number densities between 0.01 to 300 $μm^{-2}$ by molecular beam epitaxy. Subsequent overgrowth of these seed nanowires by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy yields GaN $μ$-platelets with corresponding number densities. The platelets exhibit N-polarity and form an ohmic contact to the metallic TiN substrate. By adjusting the growth conditions during the metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy, particularly the carrier gas and precursor ratio, the morphology of the GaN can be controlled across a broad range. Growth under N$_{2}$ carrier gas and with a 1:1 NH$_{3}$/trimethylgallium precursor flow ratio results in platelet ensembles with broad diameter and height distributions. In contrast, employing an N$_{2}$/H$_{2}$ carrier gas mixture promotes the formation of more homogeneous ensembles with narrower size distributions around a diameter of $\approx$2 $μm$. Finally, N-rich growth conditions under H$_{2}$ carrier gas enhance lateral growth, leading to the formation of coalesced GaN layers. GaN grown under these latter conditions exhibits strong near-band-edge emission, accompanied by only weak deep-level luminescence at room temperature.

title: Correlating orbital order and photovoltaic effect in Layered Ruddlesden-Popper Pr0.5Ca1.5MnO4 and PrCa2Mn2O7
abstract: The understanding of growth and structure-property relations of epitaxial thin films of layered Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite oxides open up new pathways to tune correlated electron properties and to fabricate new types of correlated electron junctions, such as e.g. photovoltaic devices. In particular, the layered Ruddlesden-Popper systems Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$ and PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ at half doping exhibit much higher transition temperatures for the formation of charge and orbital ordered phases of $T_c$ = 320 K and $T_c$ up to 370 K, respectively, compared to the half doped non-layered system Pr$_{1-x}$Ca$_{x}$MnO$_3$ (PCMO) with $T_c$ = 240 K. Here, we demonstrate the successful growth of epitaxial PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ thin films by ion beam sputtering and compare electric transport, optical absorbance, electronic bandstructure and photovoltaic response with epitaxial Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$, both deposited on (Nb:)SrTiO$_3$ (110) substrates. An enhanced density of Ruddlesden-Popper type of stacking faults is identified as a relaxation channel for misfit strain in PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ and seems to be the origin for the reduced $T_c$ = 320 K and the reduced spatial coherence of charge and orbital order in comparison to Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$. Since the onset of the hot polaron photovoltaic effect is correlated to the formation of charge and orbital ordering, the comparative study of temperature dependent electric transport and photovoltaic response gives insights into the different role of strain and strain relaxation related defects on photo-electric properties.

title: TotalSegmentator Aorta Report: Automated Aortic Diameter Measurement at 11 Standardized Landmarks on CT Images
abstract: Purpose: To develop and evaluate a fully automated, open-source tool that measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks from the aortic annulus to the bifurcation on any CT image, following current guideline recommendations. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 239 arterial phase CT angiography examinations of 230 patients (median age, 65 years [range, 18-99 years]; 163 men) performed between April 2025 and October 2026 (209 electrocardiographically [ECG] gated). The tool locates landmarks from TotalSegmentator segmentations of aortic branches and vertebrae and measures the maximum diameter at each. A senior radiologist reviewed and, where needed, corrected the automated measurements to create the reference standard. Agreement was assessed with mean absolute error (MAE), bias, and differences greater than 2 mm. Results: Across all landmarks, MAE was 1.06 mm (95% CI: 0.91, 1.22), and 86.6% (95% CI: 84.4, 88.5) of differences were 2 mm or less. The tool measured slightly larger diameters (bias, 0.45 mm [95% CI: 0.34, 0.57]). The sinuses of Valsalva had the largest MAE (2.17 mm [95% CI: 1.59, 2.86]). For 1.2% of landmarks, the automatic measurement failed. Examination-level MAE did not differ significantly by pathology, atherosclerosis grade (P=.95), or ECG gating (P=.14). Examinations with mural thrombus more often had an MAE greater than 2 mm (50% [95% CI: 31, 69] vs 20%; P=.03). Conclusion: The tool measured aortic diameters at 11 landmarks along the entire aorta with an MAE of about 1 mm, below published interreader variability. Agreement was lower at the aortic root and with mural thrombus. Code availability: The tool is open source and freely available at https://github.com/wasserth/TotalSegmentator.

title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
abstract: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
abstract: Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra-low-power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI. Their breakthrough eliminates a long-standing "dead layer" problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin. Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials' electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities

title: Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of antibodies is often limited by the evolution of their targets. Designing or eliciting antibodies that withstand such evolution is challenging as their binding interfaces must accommodate antigenic variation. Here, we introduce Germinal Multi, a computational framework for de novo antibody design and rescue that jointly optimizes a single paratope against multiple antigenic variants. We applied Germinal Multi to cancer and viral antigens, targeting both observed antigenic variation and prospective antibody escape. Multi-target optimization yielded antibodies that bound resistance-associated EGFR variants or that neutralized antigenically distinct historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, with recognition extending to variants withheld from the design process. Beyond acting on observed evolution, we redesigned the broadly neutralizing antibody BD55-1205 to restore neutralization of a prospective escape variant engineered with guidance from an evolutionary forecasting model, while preserving activity against the parental variant. Successful candidates were identified after screening tens of designs per campaign. Together, these results establish multi-target computational design as a strategy for generating antibody breadth across observed antigenic variation and demonstrate the potential of evolutionary forecasting to guide antibody redesign against prospective escape.

title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
abstract: Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
abstract: The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Predicting CO2 Reduction Selectivity on Large-Scale Cu–Pd Nanoparticles via a Multi-Scale Machine Learning Framework
abstract: The conventional computational approach to electrocatalyst evaluation has long been limited by its reliance on simplified slab models and adsorption energies on bare surfaces, which fail to capture the structural complexity of realistic nanoparticles (NPs) and the presence of adsorbates that decorates electrode surfaces under working conditions. To bridge this gap, we present a multi-scale computational framework that combines machine learning potential (MLP)-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with the explicit realization of potential-dependent surface coverage and high-throughput…

title: Scalar Entropic Damage Transport: Well-posed softening with a single damage variable
abstract: Entropic Damage Transport (EDT) represents material softening via a local continuum damage model while ensuring the well-posedness of the mechanical boundary value problem. It is based on a convexification of the time-incremental potential associated with a rate-limited scalar damage model. A one-dimensional distribution of damage states serves as the internal variable, and the number of these states grows with the number of time steps. We show that the emergence of the damage distribution is an artifact of the time discretization. Surprisingly, the distribution concentrates at a single damage state in the time-continuous limit, and EDT converges to a rate-limited damage model with a scalar damage variable, whose free energy is jointly convex in the strain and the reciprocal degradation. We exploit this hidden convexity by a frozen-metric discretization in terms of the reciprocal degradation, which renders every increment jointly convex. The resulting scalar update preserves damage irreversibility, the prescribed damage-rate limitation and thermomechanical consistency, reduces to a scalar equation and provides a symmetric and positive definite algorithmic tangent in closed form. Computational experiments assess the accuracy and the efficiency of both formulations from the material point to the microstructure level, and demonstrate that the scalar update permits a finite-element computation of industrial size with more than 14 million degrees of freedom.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian physics-augmented neural networks for populations of hyperelastic laws: specimen variability and uncertainty from scarce, noisy data
abstract: The hyperelastic law of a material such as soft tissue differs between specimens, and often only a few specimens can be tested. Physics-augmented neural networks (PANNs) learn such laws from data without a prescribed functional form while keeping them physically admissible, and Bayesian versions of related models quantify the uncertainty of the law of one specimen or of a pooled group of specimens. A pooled fit, however, attributes the differences between specimens to measurement noise or to uncertainty about a mean law, and neither describes a new specimen. We first develop a Bayesian PANN for one specimen, whose priors keep the learned law plausible for few, noisy data. We then extend it to a hierarchical Bayesian PANN, a nonlinear mixed-effects model in which all specimens share learned polyconvex features and each specimen is a draw from a population of laws. Features, specimens, and population are inferred jointly by variational inference, with a separate model of the measurement noise, so that the variability between specimens is not mistaken for noise, the population carries its own uncertainty, and every specimen drawn from it is polyconvex. The population predicts the response of new specimens with credible intervals, without data or from a partial test, and assigns them to cohorts with quantified uncertainty, all without a prescribed form of the law. On synthetic populations, it recovers the population from few specimens and predicts new specimens more reliably than three published methods. On Treloar's rubber and on healthy and aneurysmal aortas, it reaches the accuracy of a deterministic PANN and assigns no aorta specimen to the wrong cohort with confidence, although it underestimates the uncertainty of untested curves.

title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moiré Flatband Superconductor
abstract: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moiré flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moiré flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of $R_c =~0.62R_Q$ and finite-temperature scaling of $zν_B = 2.3$, where $R_Q = h/4e^2$ is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of $R_Q$ that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. Both the superconductor and the bosonic insulator could be driven into the same critical quantum fluctuation regime dynamically under a large bias. Our results establish moiré flatband as a clean platform for studying unconventional superconductivity and bosonic quantum criticality governed by quantum fluctuations.

title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
abstract: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically. This survey introduces a unified formalism that describes every QGNN as an encoder, a graph-conditioned circuit, observables, and an optional classical head, together with a circuit-level condition for permutation equivariance and a resource model for comparing costs. We organize the literature into five architecture families (convolutional, equivariant, message-passing and recurrent, Hamiltonian, and hybrid) and compare them by qubit cost, symmetry, scalability, and evidence. We then review symmetry and geometric inductive biases (permutation, rotation, and Lorentz), the results on expressivity, trainability, noise, and scalability, and applications in high-energy physics, chemistry, finance, healthcare, earth observation, and transportation. An audit of datasets and evaluation practices leads to a minimum reporting protocol. Our main finding is that the design space is rich and symmetry is the best-supported inductive bias, whereas the evidence remains thin: results are mostly simulated, on small graphs, at parity with classical models or with fewer parameters, and no advantage has yet been established on tasks over classical graph data. We identify five open challenges and a research agenda covering provable advantage, equivariant and geometric designs, fault-tolerant implementations, and shared benchmarks. The coverage extends through 2026 and emphasizes recent work.

title: Conformationally Locked Yttrium Indanosalan Complexes for Fast Isoselective Ring-Opening Polymerization of β-Butyrolactone at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: We report rigid yttrium indanosalan complexes for the high-temperature ring-opening polymerization of β-butyrolactone. Some of the complexes (isolated or obtained in situ) developed were able to polymerize β-butyrolactone with high isoselectivity (Pm = 0.88) and very high activity (TOF up to 135,000 h–1) at a polymerization temperature of 100 °C, at which the polymer remains in solution, facilitating its further processing. Polymerization at 30–60 °C yielded the poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s with Pm up to 0.94.

title: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
abstract: Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity.

title: TDDFT Gradients and Nonadiabatic Couplings with Minimal Auxiliary Basis Set Approximation for Fewest-Switches Surface Hopping Dynamics
abstract: The electronic structure calculations remain a major bottleneck in ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics. We develop an efficient TDDFT-based FSSH implementation in the GPU4PySCF package for medium-sized molecular systems. Our approach combines density fitting, TDDFT with minimal auxiliary basis sets (TDDFT-ris), and an approximate Z-vector solver to reduce the computational cost of TDDFT excited states and derivative coupling calculations. These approximations introduce modest changes in the relaxation time scales while maintaining high computational efficiency.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Training reservoirs without looking back
abstract: By training a reservoir computing system without access to its intermediate states and by eliminating the coupling between its nodes, a physical learning framework achieves efficient learning both in simulation and on optoelectronic hardware.

title: A perfect couple: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis
abstract: They say opposites attract, and many couples do fit this pattern. One is pragmatic and down-to-earth, while the other is a dreamer with their head in the clouds. Yet, these differences make them perfect for each other. According to researchers at ICFO, chemical interactions between atoms are not that different. Ruthenium, for instance, belongs to the "dreamer" class. It is commonly used in single-atom catalysts that speed up water electrolysis, which splits water to obtain green hydrogen.

title: Green Chemistry Institute Pharmaceutical Roundtable seeks 2027 award nominations
abstract: The four awards highlight green chemistry implementations across synthetic route design, manufacturing processes, discovery chemistry, and data science

title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
abstract: Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Computational analysis of KLF6/PDE4B-associated ferro-aging signatures and candidate drugs in benign prostatic hyperplasia
abstract: ObjectiveTo identify ferro-aging-related molecular candidates associated with epithelial states in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and thereby prioritize drug candidates for experimental testing.MethodsBulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets were integrated. Differential analysis, comparison of 113 machine-learning combinations, external validation of a unified random forest, SHAP interpretation, BPH phenotype mapping, pseudotime analysis, cell-cell communication analysis, and in silico virtual knockout were performed.

title: Depth-resolved microplastic distribution and environmental associations in the epipelagic-to-bathypelagic waters off southeastern Hainan Island, South China Sea
abstract: The vertical distribution of microplastics (MPs) below the surface ocean remains poorly constrained in the South China Sea (SCS). We investigated confirmation-corrected MP abundance, morphology, polymer composition, and environmental associations using 209 station-depth sampling units from 20 stations off southeastern Hainan, with sampling depths from the surface to 1700 m. Three replicate Niskin-bottle samples were collected at each station-depth, and station-depth means were used as the primary analytical observations. MPs occurred throughout the investigated depth range.

title: Greedy-Seeded Swarm Metaheuristics for Multi-UAV Disaster Search over CNN-Derived Priority Maps: A Budget-Matched Simulation Study
abstract: Battery-limited drone fleets must decide where to search first after an earthquake or flood. We study this decision in a reproducible simulation: a compact convolutional neural network (SARNet) turns a synthetic reconnaissance image into a per-cell search-priority map, and planners route five drones over that map to maximise a time-discounted search value. Four swarm metaheuristics—particle swarm optimization (PSO), a MAX–MIN ant system (ACO), the firefly algorithm (FA) and the grey wolf optimizer (GWO)—and two greedy-seeded variants are compared with random search, a lawnmower sweep and a…

title: Investigating the Role of Silica Coating toward Artificial Solid Electrolyte Interphase Formation for Na-Ion Anodes
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIB) are a promising cost-effective energy storage solution. However, many anode materials developed for SIB suffer from limited cycle life due to interfacial degradation processes. These lead to the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), a heterogeneous nanolayer resulting from electrolyte decomposition. The SEI is essential for stable long-term cycling; however, its continuous growth progressively decreases performance and may eventually lead to failure of the battery cell. In this work, we examine the effect of an artificial SEI made of thin SiO2 layers on Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) nanoparticles used as a SIB anode. The silica coating results in a 24% improvement in cycling stability after 150 cycles, with minimal effect on rate performance. Detailed characterization by solid-state NMR spectroscopy and electron microscopy shows that the silica layer suppresses the growth and alters the composition of the SEI, reducing the formation of inorganic species, particularly NaF and NaF-rich components. Using dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP)-enhanced NMR, a technique that greatly boosts NMR sensitivity, we show how the coating alters the SEI structure, from a layered inorganic core with an organic shell on uncoated LTO to a mixed mosaic-like SEI. Furthermore, we find SEI formation beneath the SiO2 layer, providing molecular-level insights into the interfacial processes. This study provides routes for the design of improved SEI layers, paving the way for the development of more durable and high-performance SIB cells for future energy storage applications.

title: Component-conditioned response residual learning framework for organic-soil component quantification using vis-NIR spectroscopy.
abstract: Visible and near-infrared reflectance (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy provides a rapid and nondestructive approach to quantitative analysis. However, existing models emphasize predictive accuracy while offering limited band-level interpretability of internal model responses. The paper addressed how continuous soil component contents could be transformed into band-level response patterns, constraining models to achieve accurate prediction and spectral interpretability. A component-conditioned response residual (CCRR) learning framework was proposed.
venue: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy

title: Engineering Organelle-Directed DNA Nanodevices: Progress, Pitfalls, and Therapeutic Promise
abstract: Organelle-level precision can advance cancer nanomedicine beyond nonspecific intracellular delivery toward spatially defined therapeutic action. DNA nanoframeworks, nanodevices, and nanomachines are promising because their sequence, geometry, valency, and dynamic states can be programmed to integrate molecular recognition with sensing, computation, structural reconfiguration, and cargo release.

title: Biochemical reassessment of the activation of PANK1 by SGLT2 inhibitors
abstract: Although SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) show cardiovascular benefits in addition to glycemic control, their molecular target for cardiovascular effect remains unclear. A recent study reported that two SGLT2i, empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, directly activate pantothenate kinase 1 (PANK1), which mediate their cardioprotective effect. PANK1 phosphorylates pantothenate with ATP to yield 4'-phosphopantothenate and ADP, representing the rate-limiting enzyme of coenzyme A (CoA) biosynthesis. We therefore reassessed this claim using purified recombinant human PANK1. The malachite green assay detected free inorganic phosphate (Pi) but neither ADP nor 4'-phosphopantothenate and its signals do not reflect PANK1 activity. In the ADP-Glo assay, empagliflozin and dapagliflozin did not stimulate PANK1 under either basal conditions or acetyl-CoA feedback inhibition, while the activator PZ-2891 enhanced the activity of PANK1. These results show that SGLT2i do not directly activate PANK1, challenging the proposed PANK1-dependent cardioprotection mechanism.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
abstract: The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A molecular glue degrader-antibody conjugate for HER2-targeted cyclin K degradation
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 12 (CDK12) is an attractive therapeutic target due to its critical role in transcriptional regulation and DNA damage response and is frequently co-amplified with ERBB2 (HER2) in breast cancer. CDK12 forms an active complex with its obligate partner cyclin K (CCNK), and pharmacological degradation of CCNK has emerged as a promising strategy for disrupting CDK12-dependent transcriptional programs. However, the broad expression and essential functions of the CDK12/CCNK complex may limit the therapeutic window of highly potent molecular glue degraders. Here, we investigate whether antibody-mediated delivery can impart cellular selectivity to a molecular glue degrader through targeting the HER2 receptor. Molecular glues lack the modular architecture of PROTACs, thus linker placement can be the central design problem. We designed SAS1001, a CCNK molecular glue degrader with a solvent-exposed piperazine primed for linker attachment. SAS1001 induced potent and ubiquitin-proteasome system-dependent degradation of CCNK and inhibited proliferation in a range of breast cancer cells. Conjugation to trastuzumab (Tz) generated the HER2-targeted degrader-antibody conjugate Tz-SS2009, which internalized preferentially in HER2-positive cells and produced enhanced CCNK degradation and antiproliferative effects, relative both to HER2-negative cells and to an isotype-matched non-targeting conjugate. Whole proteome analysis further demonstrated CCNK depletion and revealed downstream changes consistent with established roles of the CDK12/CCNK complex in transcriptional regulation. These findings demonstrate that antibody-mediated delivery can redistribute the cellular activity of a potent molecular glue degrader towards antigen-positive cells. In the CR8/DS18 purine series, substitution at a solvent-exposed position preserved CCNK degradation when the degrader was delivered on a full-length IgG. More broadly, this work extends antibody-directed degradation beyond the CRBN-based glues that have dominated the field and illustrates how structural characterization of a glue scaffold can identify a linker attachment point that does not compromise activity.

title: Tuning the Molecular Electronic Structure of Polysaccharides: A Comparative DFT Study of Chemically Modified Chitosan and Cellulose Derivatives
abstract: The rational molecular design of functionalized polysaccharides for advanced electronic and sensing applications necessitates a comprehensive mapping of their electronic chemical space. In this study, we report a high-throughput computational screening of 115 chemically modified chitosan and cellulose derivatives. Frontier molecular orbital (FMO) energies, HOMO–LUMO energy gaps (ΔE gap ), and a comprehensive suite of global conceptual density functional theory (DFT) descriptors were computed for isolated oligomeric models at the B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) level with SMD implicit solvation.

title: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
abstract: Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
abstract: Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Experimental and computational mapping reveals preferential nanobody targeting of the intracellular cavity of the amino acid transporter BasC
abstract: Nanobodies are valuable tools for stabilizing and investigating membrane transporters, but the systematic characterization of large nanobody collections remains experimentally demanding. Here, we combined biochemical and transport assays, experimental structural data and AlphaFold3 modelling to characterize a repertoire of 29 nanobodies targeting the bacterial amino acid transporter BasC. By exploiting the random orientation and asymmetric apparent substrate affinities of BasC in proteoliposomes, comparison of nanobody-mediated influx and efflux inhibition enabled experimental assignment of binding sidedness. The collection showed a marked bias towards inhibition from the intracellular face, whereas only two, Nb58 and Nb78, were identified as extracellular binders. Compatibility assays and a 6.1 [A] crystallographic map of the BasC-Nb53-Nb58 complex supported the simultaneous binding of Nb53 and Nb58 to opposite sides of the transporter and validated the functional sidedness assignment. AlphaFold3 generated high-confidence interaction models for 16 of the 29 complexes. Ten of these models targeted the large intracellular cavity, revealing recurrent epitope clusters. The predicted binding modes of Nb53, Nb71 and Nb74 agreed with available experimental structures, supporting the accuracy of these predictions. Notably, these three nanobodies had previously provided the most informative structural and smFRET data. Our results show that transport-based sidedness measurements together with confidence-filtered structural predictions can define the functional and structural landscape of a nanobody repertoire. This integrated approach may provide a virtual structural screening strategy to prioritize nanobodies, identify dominant epitope regions and select potentially compatible combinations for experimental and structural studies.

title: High Temperature Acetylene-to-Ethylene Hydrogenation over Pd: A Combined Experimental, Machine Learning Potential, and DFT Investigation
abstract: Selective hydrogenation of acetylene to ethylene at temperatures relevant to direct non-oxidative methane conversion (DNMC) could enable downstream upgrading without intermediate cooling and reheating. Here, we combine experimental catalyst screening, machine learning potential (MLP) simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to identify Pd surface motifs responsible for acetylene hydrogenation at 850°C.

title: Synergistic Construction of Axial and Central Chirality via an Organocatalytic Three-Component Reaction Involving In Situ-Formed α-Functionalized Alcohols
abstract: The synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality represents a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an organocatalytic three-component reaction among N-aryl-2-substituted anilines, 2-oxo-2-arylacetaldehydes, and indoles, which enables the de novo synthesis of axially and centrally chiral N-(2-substituted phenyl)benzo[e]indol-1-ones. This transformation features the in situ formation of α-functionalized alcohols, followed by a 1,2-addition of the resulting iminium species.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Machine learning-driven SERS platform for rapid detection and multi-analyte discrimination
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) has attracted considerable research attention owing to its outstanding capability for molecular identification, even at the single-molecule level. However, the selective identification of analyte molecules in real-world environments, such as in food and water sources, remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of a flexible, plasmonic nanopyramid array on a laminating polymer film using an inverted nanopyramid array on a silicon master mold.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Phosphonylation of Aliphatic Carboxylic Acids with Succinimidyl Phosphites as Bifunctional Reagents
abstract: Aliphatic carboxylic acids are abundant, stable, and cost-effective, rendering them ideal substrates for site-specific C(sp3)–P bond formation via decarboxylative pathways. However, the direct catalytic decarboxylative phosphonylation of these acids remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report that the use of dialkyl succinimidyl phosphites as bifunctional reagents enables the iron-catalyzed decarboxylative phosphonylation of aliphatic carboxylic acids to proceed smoothly at room temperature under visible light irradiation.

title: Redox-Responsive 2′-OH Acylation for Late-Stage RNA Conjugation
abstract: Covalent RNA conjugates have proved effective in basic research and therapy, yet their broader use is limited by synthetic complexity and high costs. Here, we describe a modular, redox-responsive strategy for late-stage conjugation of diverse biofunctional ligands onto RNA. We show that acylation of RNA 2′-OH groups with disulfide-containing acyl moieties enables thiol–disulfide exchange with thiol-bearing ligands, including N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc), peptides, biotin, and captopril.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
